title: Grateful Dead Live at McGaw Memorial Hall, Northwestern U. on 1973-11-01
lineage: SBDMR> Cass> DAT> CDR> EAC> Soundforge> DePopper> SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of a stellar second set featuring Morning Dew, Playing In The Band, Uncle John’s Band and Wharf Rat.
ai_review.review: The recording is a clean soundboard source that conveys the power of the band’s famous Wall‑of‑Sound era.  Reviewers rave about the flowing second‑set sandwich (Morning Dew → Playing In The Band → Uncle John’s Band) and highlight Garcia’s “unbelievable” guitar work, Phil’s prominent bass, and Bill’s jazzy drumming.  Aside from a brief gap before “Fly Away,” the set is praised as high‑energy and flawless.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen reviews, most 5‑star, consistently praise both performance and sound quality; only minor technical quibbles are noted.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, natural mix with the characteristic Wall‑of‑Sound presence; a short 10–20 s gap before “Fly Away” and missing first set are the only drawbacks.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Second set flows seamlessly with natural transitions – the classic Dew → Playing sandwich leads into extended jams and a powerful Wharf Rat climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's playing described as "unbelievable" and tight; his vocal on Wharf Rat noted as strong.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is high in the mix – “Phil Zone” praised, with several reviewers calling it prominent and powerful.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocals are more prominent than usual; an anecdote about a corneal abrasion is mentioned but no criticism of his playing.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann delivers a jazzy groove on Mississippi Half‑Step, noted as a highlight compared to later drumming styles.
